stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a reason for building the dam in the beginning?

options.A: To promote tourism.
options.B: To support agriculture.
options.C: To generate electricity.
options.D: To prevent natural disasters.

ev.t: a dam that would control floods, provide irrigation water, and produce hydroelectric power

note: 題目問當初興建水壩的理由，哪一個沒有提到。第 2 段說當初評估興建水壩，是為了防洪（control floods），是 (D) 防止天然災害；提供灌溉用水（provide irrigation water），是 (B) 支援農業；水力發電（produce hydroelectric power），是 (C) 發電。第 4 段雖然說胡佛水壩每年吸引一百多萬名遊客，但那是今天的情況，不是當初興建的理由，所以選 (A)。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about Hoover Dam?

options.A: Its construction lasted for more than a decade.
options.B: It is strong in functionality, but plain in design.
options.C: Its site stretches over two states in the United States.
options.D: It became famous because it led to the discovery of Black Canyon.

ev.t: Located in Black Canyon straddling the border between Nevada and Arizona

note: 第 1 段說胡佛水壩所在的黑峽谷橫跨內華達州和亞利桑那州的州界（straddling the border between Nevada and Arizona），選項換成 stretches over two states，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 Black Canyon，原文沒有說水壩讓人發現了黑峽谷，第 2 段說早在 1900 年左右就有人在評估黑峽谷；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 plain，太平淡的是最初的設計，後來已經請建築師重新設計；(A) 水壩在 1931 年到 1936 年興建，只花了五年左右，不到十年。
map: straddling the border between Nevada and Arizona

stem: According to the passage, what did Six Companies, Inc. experience in the process of building the dam?

options.A: It was defeated by the harsh working conditions.
options.B: It lost some workers in the construction of the dam.
options.C: It benefited from prior experience of building dams of similar scale.
options.D: It gave up the project authorized by the government before the deadline.

ev.t: cost over one hundred lives
The winning bid to build the dam was submitted by Six Companies, Inc.

note: 這一題要把兩段合起來看。第 1 段說興建工程有超過一百人喪命（cost over one hundred lives），第 2 段說得標興建水壩的就是 Six Companies，所以 Six Companies 在興建過程中失去了一些工人，是 (B)。(A) 第 2 段雖然說夏天酷熱、工地缺乏設施，但接著用 Nevertheless 轉折，說 Six Companies 還是完工了，可見並沒有因為困難而放棄；(C) 原文說這麼大的混凝土結構以前沒有人蓋過，所以不可能有類似規模的經驗；(D) 照抄 authorized，國會核准的工程 Six Companies 並沒有放棄，反而提早兩年多完工。

stem: What contribution did Gordon B. Kaufmann make to Hoover Dam?

options.A: He improved the outer appearance of the dam.
options.B: He enhanced the practical functions of the dam.
options.C: He added aboriginal flavor to the design of the floor.
options.D: He decorated the walls of the dam with images from nature.

ev.t: the architect who was brought in to redesign the exterior

note: 第 3 段說最初的設計太平淡，所以請建築師 Kaufmann 重新設計外觀（redesign the exterior），選項換成 improved the outer appearance，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 walls、(C) 照抄 floor，負責牆面和地板裝飾、融入美洲原住民圖像的是插畫家 Allen Tupper True，不是 Kaufmann；(B) 原文說最初的設計太重視功能，Kaufmann 改的是外觀，不是實用功能。

stem: According to the passage, where does the word “restaurant” originate from?

options.A: Famous chefs.
options.B: Popular soups.
options.C: Dining halls.
options.D: Daily menus.

ev.t: the merchant class of Paris developed a taste for healthy clear broths which were considered restorative; hence the term

note: 第 2 段說 1760 年代巴黎的商人愛上了健康的清湯（clear broths），大家認為這種湯能恢復元氣（restorative），hence（因此）restaurant 這個字就是這樣來的。hence 表示這個字是從前面那句來的，前面那句講的是大家都愛喝的清湯，broth 就是湯，選項換成 popular soups，所以是 (B)。restorative 和 restaurant 拼法相近，也看得出兩個字的關係。(C) 照抄 dining halls，1780 年代出現的有名餐廳，是清湯熱潮帶來的結果，不是這個字的來源；(A) 照抄 chefs，中世紀有私人廚師的是貴族，和這個字的來源無關；(D) 原文沒有提到菜單。

stem: What does “taken their toll on kitchen tables” mean in the third paragraph?

options.A: Deprived people of adequate food for living.
options.B: Controlled the nutrients in people’s diet.
options.C: Charged people for using kitchen tables.
options.D: Paid tribute to chefs working in kitchens.

ev.t: the majority of the French population could not afford bread
By 1789, the starving French masses could no longer be controlled.

note: take a toll on 是「對……造成嚴重的不良影響」，kitchen tables 指每戶人家的餐桌，也就是一般人家吃的東西。前一句說大多數法國人連麵包都買不起（could not afford bread），後面又說飢餓的群眾（the starving French masses）失控，可見嚴冬和苛稅讓人民沒有足夠的食物，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 kitchen tables，toll 雖然也有「通行費」的意思，但這裡不是說使用餐桌要收費；(D) 照抄 chefs，第 3 段的廚師是貴族留下來的，和這句話無關；(B) 原文沒有提到營養。

stem: Which of the following is true about commercial diners before the French Revolution?

options.A: Many fine restaurants were owned by highly skilled chefs.
options.B: Reputable dining halls were popular in Paris during the 1760s.
options.C: Public dining halls in the Middle Ages were run-down and dirty.
options.D: A limited variety of food was served in Parisian restaurants in the 1780s.

ev.t: The only commercial diners for the masses were dusty, shabby roadside inns

note: 第 2 段說中世紀時，一般大眾唯一能去的營業用餐處所，是塵土滿布（dusty）、破舊簡陋（shabby）的路邊旅店，選項換成 run-down and dirty，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 Reputable dining halls，有名的餐廳是 1780 年代才出現的，1760 年代巴黎商人才剛愛上清湯；(D) 照抄 1780s，原文說那時候的餐廳可以從許多菜色中挑選，菜色不是有限；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 highly skilled chefs，技術高超的廚師原本替貴族工作，大革命以後才流向城裡的餐館，原文也沒有說餐廳是廚師開的。

stem: What was the main reason for Napoleon to promote the development of restaurants?

options.A: He hoped to improve the life of his citizens.
options.B: He wanted to help unemployed chefs find new jobs.
options.C: He feared that reductions in restaurants might hurt the travel business.
options.D: He believed that the development of restaurants would bring political stability.

ev.t: as he reasoned that people who were focused on champagne and fine food probably would not conspire against him

note: 第 4 段說拿破崙給公民「享樂的自由」，因為他認為一心想著香檳和美食的人，大概不會密謀推翻他（would not conspire against him）。沒有人密謀推翻他，政權就穩定，所以是 (D)。(A) 讓公民享樂看起來像是為人民著想，但原文用 as 點出真正的理由是保住自己的政權；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 unemployed，失業的廚師進城開店是大革命時期的事，在拿破崙掌權以前；(C) 照抄 travel，旅遊指南只是用來說明餐廳的數量增加，原文沒有提到餐廳減少會影響旅遊業。

stem: What makes falcons a unique animal for hunting in Islamic culture?

options.A: Falcons are relatively easy to train for hunting.
options.B: Falcons can form a strong bond with their owners quickly.
options.C: Falcons’ vision is particularly suitable for hunting in deserts.
options.D: Falcons keep their prey alive before delivering it to falconers.

ev.t: they can be trained to deliver their prey, without killing it first.
animals used for food must still be alive

note: 第 3 段說獵鷹經過訓練，可以把獵物帶回來，不先殺死（without killing it first），這在伊斯蘭文化很重要，因為當作食物的動物必須還活著，肉才是清真的。選項換成 keep their prey alive，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 vision，獵鷹的視力是人類的 2.6 倍，但這和伊斯蘭文化的規定無關；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 strong，緊密的關係是鷹獵者日夜和獵鷹住在一起建立的，原文沒有說很快就能建立；(A) 第 2 段說先不給食物，是讓獵鷹比較容易馴服，原文沒有說獵鷹本來就比較好訓練，也和伊斯蘭文化無關。

stem: What is the main reason for Arabic people to hunt with falcons today?

options.A: To supplement their diet.
options.B: To serve as entertainment and exercise.
options.C: To worship their national bird.
options.D: To replace the practice of hunting with dogs.

ev.t: But now, it has become the favorite sport and pastime in the Arabian Peninsula.

note: 第 1 段說鷹獵過去是為了補充食物，But now（不過現在）已經成為阿拉伯半島最受歡迎的運動（sport）和休閒活動（pastime），選項換成 entertainment and exercise，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 supplement，補充食物是過去的目的，題目問的是今天（today）；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 national bird，有些國家把獵鷹定為國鳥，原文沒有說打獵是為了崇拜國鳥；(D) 照抄 dogs，「天空獵犬」（hunting dogs of the skies）是比喻獵鷹的說法，原文沒有說用獵鷹取代獵犬。

stem: According to the article, what privilege do falcons enjoy in the Arab world?

options.A: Free air ticket.
options.B: Passports issued by the King.
options.C: Meals that are halal.
options.D: Access to specialized medical care.

ev.t: specialist hospitals have been established to take care of these magnificent birds

note: 第 4 段說鷹獵越來越受歡迎，甚至有專門照顧獵鷹的醫院（specialist hospitals），選項換成 specialized medical care，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (B)，這個選項照抄 Passports，但原文只說獵鷹還能領到自己的護照（are even issued their own passports），沒有說護照是誰發的，選項加上的 by the King，原文沒有這個資訊。(C) 照抄第 3 段的 halal，清真講的是獵鷹抓回來、要給人吃的獵物，不是獵鷹自己吃的餐點；(A) 原文說獵鷹可以合法搭飛機、待在機艙裡，沒有說機票免費。

stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Falconers deprive the falcons of food in order to capture them.
options.B: Falcons are not allowed to see their masters during the training process.
options.C: The trainers’ names are imprinted on the hoods covering the birds’ heads.
options.D: Wild falcons with natural hunting skills are most ideal for falconers to catch.

ev.t: The best birds to catch are the ones with naturally nurtured hunting skills, aged one or two years.

note: 第 2 段說最適合捕捉的（The best birds to catch）是一、兩歲、天生就有狩獵本領（naturally nurtured hunting skills）的獵鷹，選項換成 most ideal for falconers to catch，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 of food，不給食物是捉到以後的訓練步驟，目的是讓獵鷹容易馴服，不是為了捕捉；(C) 照抄 imprint，原文的 imprint 是獵鷹把第一眼看到的人認作主人，不是把名字印在頭罩上；(B) 照抄 master，原文說鷹獵者日夜和獵鷹住在一起，訓練時並沒有不讓獵鷹看到主人。
map: most ideal for falconers to catch

stem: Which of the following best states the main idea of the first paragraph?

options.A: Science and technology have influenced the game of golf.
options.B: Price, durability, and function determine the quality of golf balls.
options.C: Accumulated efforts have resulted in changes in how golf balls are made.
options.D: Golfers who have a sound knowledge of aerodynamics play the game well.

ev.t: many advances have occurred in the game, including significant changes to the golf ball.

note: 第 1 段第一句說高爾夫球這項運動有了許多進步，其中包括球本身的重大改變（significant changes to the golf ball），接著依時間順序介紹木球、羽毛球、古塔膠球、Haskell 球、有凹洞的球，一直到現在的球。一代一代累積的改良，改變了球的製作方式，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 aerodynamics，空氣動力是第 2 段的內容，第 1 段沒有談；(A) 科學和科技影響高爾夫球運動，說得太籠統，第 1 段只談球的演進；(B) 價格、耐用度只是用來比較各代的球，第 1 段沒有說這些條件決定球的品質。
map: significant changes to the golf ball
changes in how golf balls are made

stem: Which of the following is true about golf balls?

options.A: William Taylor added a rubber center to golf balls.
options.B: The Gutta Percha ball was stuffed with bird feathers.
options.C: The Featherie was the first golf ball ever used in the game.
options.D: The Haskell lasted longer and traveled farther than its predecessor.

ev.t: The Haskell traveled up to 20 yards farther than the Gutta Percha ball and was more durable.

note: 第 1 段說 Haskell 球比之前的古塔膠球多飛 20 碼（traveled up to 20 yards farther），也更耐用（more durable），選項換成 lasted longer and traveled farther than its predecessor，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 rubber，第一顆有橡膠核心的是 Haskell 球，William Taylor 推出的是第一顆有凹洞的球；(B) 照抄 feathers，塞羽毛的是羽毛球，古塔膠球的原料是古塔樹葉子的汁液；(C) 照抄 Featherie，羽毛球之前已經有圓形木球，羽毛球不是最早的高爾夫球。

stem: How do dimples on a golf ball affect its performance?

options.A: They help it travel farther.
options.B: They keep it in a better shape.
options.C: They enhance its drag force.
options.D: They allow it to endure stronger impact.

ev.t: With dimples added to the ball, the force that pulls back on the ball is minimized, allowing it to travel faster and longer.

note: 第 2 段說球加上凹洞以後，往後拉的力量減到最小，讓球飛得更快、更遠（travel faster and longer），選項換成 travel farther，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 drag，往後拉的力量就是阻力（drag），凹洞把阻力減到最小，選項說增加阻力，剛好相反；(B) 保持形狀、(D) 承受更強的撞擊，原文都沒有提到。

stem: Which ball will give golfers a better shot to get a ball out of a deep sand trap?

options.A: A ball with deep dimples.
options.B: A ball made from Gutta trees.
options.C: A ball with a leather sack.
options.D: A ball with a smooth outer cover.

ev.t: whereas those with deeper dimples have a higher flight path.

note: 球掉進很深的沙坑，要讓球飛得高，才打得出來。第 2 段說凹洞比較深的球（deeper dimples），飛行路徑比較高，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 1 段的 Gutta、(C) 照抄 leather sack，古塔膠球和塞羽毛的皮囊球都是舊式的球，原文沒有說它們適合打沙坑；(D) 照抄 outer cover，Haskell 球有外殼，但原文說凹洞才影響飛行高度，表面光滑的球沒有凹洞的好處。

stem: Who is most likely the writer of this passage?

options.A: The President of the University of Illinois.
options.B: A movie critic who is a friend of the Eberts.
options.C: A member of the Festival’s organizing committee.
options.D: A journalist who reports stories about the Festival.

ev.t: In selecting the films for this year, Chaz Ebert and I looked to women filmmakers for our inspiration.
We would like to thank our sponsors, volunteers, festival pass holders, and individual ticket holders

note: 作者在第 2 段說今年選片時，Chaz Ebert 和我（Chaz Ebert and I）以女性電影人作為靈感，可見作者負責挑選影片；第 4 段又代表影展感謝贊助者、志工和觀眾，全文也一直用 our festival、we 這樣的說法。會選片、會代表影展致謝的，最可能是影展籌備委員會的成員，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 University of Illinois，作者是在感謝伊利諾大學，不是代表大學說話；(D) 記者是報導影展的外人，不會說「我們的影展」；(B) 作者說能和伊伯特夫婦合作是一種榮幸，是合作的關係，原文沒有說作者是影評人。

stem: What was the purpose of reinventing Roger Ebert’s Film Festival in 1999?

options.A: To work closely with the University of Illinois.
options.B: To help restore a building associated with the Festival.
options.C: To establish a signature annual event in the community.
options.D: To honor people who made films that were not box-office hits.

ev.t: to make a festival that celebrated overlooked films, formats and genres, and the women and men who made those films

note: 第 1 段說 1999 年重新打造影展，是要表揚受到忽略的電影（overlooked films），以及拍出這些電影的人。受到忽略的電影，就是票房不好、沒有受到注意的片子，所以是 (D)。這一句是倒裝：Little did we think（我們萬萬沒想到）後面接的，是當初沒有料到的結果，不是目的。(C) 照抄 annual event，成為社區的年度盛事，(B) 幫忙修復 Virginia 戲院，都是當時沒有料到的結果；(A) 照抄 University of Illinois，伊利諾大學媒體學院是合作單位，原文沒有說合作是重新打造影展的目的。

stem: What is the focus of this year’s film selection?

options.A: Films produced or directed by women.
options.B: Hollywood classics and legends.
options.C: Stories featuring female leading roles.
options.D: Diversity in formats and genres.

ev.t: Chaz Ebert and I looked to women filmmakers for our inspiration.
Fully half of our films are either directed or co-directed by women, and several others have women in powerful producing roles.

note: 第 2 段說今年選片以女性電影人（women filmmakers）作為靈感，一半的影片由女性執導或共同執導，還有好幾部由女性擔任製片，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 roles，原文的 producing roles 是幕後的製片工作，不是片中的女主角；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 Hollywood，好萊塢傳奇人物 Jeff Dowd 是嘉賓，不是選片重點；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 formats and genres，那是 1999 年重新打造影展時要表揚的對象，不是今年選片的重點。

stem: Which of the following is NOT included in the writer’s acknowledgement remarks?

options.A: The founder of Roger Ebert’s Film Festival.
options.B: A student who purchased a pass to the Festival.
options.C: The producer of the Festival’s award-winning film.
options.D: A company which provided financial support for the Festival.

ev.t: We would like to thank our sponsors, volunteers, festival pass holders, and individual ticket holders
for that we thank him and his wife Chaz.

note: 作者在第 4、5 段致謝。感謝贊助者（sponsors），是 (D) 出錢支持影展的公司；感謝影展通行證持有人（festival pass holders），買了通行證的學生也在其中，是 (B)；第 5 段感謝羅傑·伊伯特，影展是他送給家鄉的禮物，他就是 (A) 影展的創辦人。第 2 段雖然提到幾位女性製片，但那是介紹今年的選片，不是致謝，原文也沒有提到哪一部片子得獎，所以選 (C)。

stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?

options.A: General facts regarding storm chasing.
options.B: Common equipment used by storm chasers.
options.C: Shared characteristics among storm chasers.
options.D: Meteorological knowledge crucial to storm chasing.

ev.t: Chasing often involves driving thousands of miles in order to witness a relatively short window of time of severe weather.
The amount of equipment used for storm chasing also varies.

note: 第 2 段講了好幾件追風暴的一般情況：常要開幾千英里的車，空手而回並不少見；大部分人不是專業的氣象學家；使用的裝備多寡也各不相同。這一段介紹的是追風暴的一般事實，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 equipment，裝備只是這一段的其中一件事；(D) 氣象學也只占一句，原文是說很多人花時間自學，不是在介紹氣象知識；(C) 這一段反而一再說各人不同，有人只帶攝影器材，有人什麼都用上，講的不是共同點。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about chasing severe weather?

options.A: The danger of chasing tornadoes can be avoided.
options.B: Those who chase storms share one common reason.
options.C: There is a standard set of equipment for storm chasing.

options.B: The original meaning of haka in Māori is a war dance accompanied by songs.
options.C: The All Blacks have taken turns performing Ka Mate and Kapa o Pango since 1906.
options.D: Haka are now used for important events by both Māori and non-Māori New Zealanders.

ev.t: different varieties of haka are performed on various ceremonial occasions
and New Zealanders of European heritage alike view doing the haka with a sense of pride

note: 最後一段說現在哈卡在迎接貴賓、婚禮、葬禮等典禮場合（ceremonial occasions）表演，而且毛利人和歐洲裔的紐西蘭人（New Zealanders of European heritage）都以跳哈卡為榮。選項把典禮場合換成 important events，把歐洲裔的紐西蘭人換成 non-Māori New Zealanders，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄最後一段的 limited to，傳統上只限於毛利社群，不是只限男性戰士，第 2 段還說有些哈卡男女都能跳，甚至有只限女性的；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 war dance，那是一般人的看法，接著 But 一轉，說在毛利語中 haka 只是「舞蹈」的意思；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 1906，1906 年全黑隊第一次表演的是 Ka Mate，Kapa o Pango 是 2005 年才寫的，不可能從 1906 年起就輪流表演。

stem: Which of the following is the best title for this passage?

options.A: Computers and Assessments
options.B: The Four Components of ESSA
options.C: Student-Centered Curriculum and Instruction
options.D: From NCLB to ESSA, with a Focus on Assessment

note: 第 1 段先說 ESSA 取代了 NCLB，讓各州在課程、教學、評量上有更多決定權，最後一句說 Below are some big-picture ideas influencing many states as they approach the assessment task，點出後面要談的是各州規劃評量（assessment）的方向；第 2 到 5 段依序談彈性、多科目測驗、重視學習過程、評量的目的，四段都在講評量。標題要同時涵蓋從 NCLB 換成 ESSA，以及談的重點是評量，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (B)：後面四段是影響各州的四個大方向（ideas influencing many states），不是 ESSA 這個法案的四個組成部分，偏離主題。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 student-centered，全文談的是評量，不是課程和教學，偏離主題；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 computer，電腦適性測驗只是第 2 段舉的例子，過於狹隘。

stem: What does the word “dilemma” in paragraph 2 refer to?

options.A: The choice between SAT and ACT.
options.B: The choice between NCLB and ESSA.
options.C: Whether or not to use student-centered assessment.
options.D: Whether or not to replace computer-based assessment.

ev.t: Thus, states are rethinking one-size-fits-all standardized assessments and are instead considering personalized, student-centered assessments in schools.
Obviously, the task is difficult and time-consuming.

note: 第 2 段先說標準化評量容易使用，卻無法完整呈現學生的進展，所以各州考慮改用以學生為中心的評量（student-centered assessments）；接著說這項工作既困難又費時。一邊是比較完整的評量，一邊是做起來很難，要不要採用以學生為中心的評量，就是這裡的 dilemma（難題），所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 SAT and ACT，那是拿來比喻標準化評量的例子，不是要在兩者之間做選擇；(D) 照抄 computer，電腦適性測驗是解決難題的方法，不是難題本身；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 NCLB，2015 年 ESSA 就已經取代了 NCLB，這是已經決定的事。

It was discovered during tofu production when discarded soybean residue caught microbial spores from the air and grew certain whitish fungi around it.

options.A: By giving a definition.
options.B: By mentioning an incident.
options.C: By providing statistics.

ev.t: When Dr. David Spiegel emerged from a three-hour shoulder surgery in 1972

note: 第 1 段一開頭講一件事：1972 年 Spiegel 醫師動完肩部手術，沒有用止痛藥，而是替自己催眠，結果真的有效。作者用一件實際發生的事開場，引出催眠這個主題，所以是 (B)。(A) 催眠的定義在第 2 段才出現；(C) 第 4 段才有止痛藥用量減半的研究結果，開頭沒有統計數字；(D) 比較兩組人的反應是第 3 段的研究。

stem: According to the passage, what is the goal of Dr. Spiegel’s work?

options.A: To explain the real cause of pain.
options.B: To help people concentrate on their job.
options.C: To explore how hypnosis can be used as a medical treatment.
options.D: To strengthen the brain’s functions to reduce psychological problems.

ev.t: This trance-like state can be an effective tool to control pain, ease anxiety, and deal with stress.
Spiegel hopes that the practice can be used to replace painkillers.

note: 第 2 段說催眠是控制疼痛、緩解焦慮、應付壓力的有效工具；第 4 段說 Spiegel 希望催眠可以用來取代止痛藥（replace painkillers），還研究了自我催眠能讓病人少用一半的止痛藥。他研究的是催眠怎麼當作醫療方法，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 pain，他研究的是用催眠減輕疼痛，不是找出疼痛的原因；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 brain，研究人員只是觀察到催眠時大腦的變化，沒有說要強化大腦的功能；(B) 第 2 段的專注是說明催眠時的狀態，不是要幫人專心工作。

stem: According to Dr. Spiegel, which of the following is true when people are hypnotized?

options.A: They recall only happy memories.
options.B: Their mind is fixed only on what they are doing.
options.C: They do whatever they are told to do.
options.D: They have greater awareness of things around them.

ev.t: You focus intently on the subject at hand, to the near exclusion of any other thought.

note: 第 2 段先說一般人的誤解（is often misunderstood as），再用 But according to Dr. Spiegel 帶出他的看法。題目問的是 According to Dr. Spiegel，答案要在 But 後面找：催眠時你會全神貫注在眼前的事情上（focus intently on the subject at hand），幾乎不去想別的事，選項換成 Their mind is fixed only on what they are doing，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 whatever，別人叫你做什麼就做什麼，是 But 前面一般人的誤解；(D) 照抄 around，原文說催眠時會把周遭（around you）大部分的刺激屏除在外，選項說更能察覺周遭的事物，意思正好相反；(A) 第 3 段的回想記憶，是研究中掃描大腦的其中一種情況，不是催眠時的狀態，原文也沒有提到快樂的記憶。
map: focus intently on the subject at hand
fixed only on what they are doing

stem: What can be inferred about highly hypnotizable people?

options.A: They tend to be isolated from the society.
options.B: They are more likely to fall asleep during the day.
options.C: They may easily identify themselves with characters in fictions.
options.D: They are more trustworthy than people who are less hypnotizable.

ev.t: more likely to get caught up in a good movie.

note: 第 3 段說容易催眠的人，看到一部好電影，比較容易沉浸其中（get caught up in a good movie）。看電影容易入戲，就是容易把自己投入片中角色的處境，電影也是虛構的故事，選項換成 identify themselves with characters in fictions，所以是 (C)。最容易選錯的是 (D)，這個選項照抄 trust：原文說的是容易催眠的人比較信任別人（more trusting of others），trusting 是「信任別人」，選項的 trustworthy 是「值得別人信任」，兩個字意思不同。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 sleep，把催眠當成睡著，正是 Spiegel 說的誤解；(A) 容易催眠的人比較信任別人，看不出他們和社會隔絕。
map: caught up in a good movie

stem: What is the purpose of this passage?

options.A: To evaluate the languages used by different ethnic groups.
options.B: To prove how civilization slows down language development.
options.C: To describe how terms of smell are found in different languages.
options.D: To point out the link between language use and the environment.

note: 第 1、2 段比較英語和 Maniq 語、Jahai 語描述氣味的詞彙；第 3 段說英語的困難和鼻子的能力無關，研究人員認為是環境的關係；第 4 段說明兩種生活環境的差異，最後說這個差異或許能解釋這個語言現象。全文要指出的是語言使用和環境之間的關係，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 terms，介紹各種語言有多少氣味詞彙，只是第 2 段的內容，全文還要解釋原因，過於狹隘；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 ethnic groups，原文沒有評價哪一種語言比較好，偏離主題；(B) 原文說英語使用者不必靠氣味生存，沒有說文明讓語言發展變慢，偏離主題。

stem: What does the word “want” in the first paragraph most likely mean?

options.A: Lack.
options.B: Growth.
options.C: Loss.
options.D: Search.

ev.t: For want of dedicated odor terminology, English speakers are often forced to use odor-sources

note: for want of 是固定片語，意思是「因為缺少」，want 在這裡當名詞用。從上下文也推得出來：第 1 段第一句說英語沒有直截了當談論氣味的方法，後面說英語使用者只好（are forced to）借用氣味的來源和比喻。只好借用別的說法，是因為缺少專門的氣味詞彙，所以 want 最接近 (A) Lack。(C) Loss 是「失去」，表示原本有、後來沒了，原文沒有說英語曾經有這些詞彙；(B) 成長、(D) 尋找，都接不上後面的「只好借用」。

options.B: Their ability to smell is stronger than that of the Jahai.
options.C: They use smell terms to describe how food looks and tastes.
options.D: Their living environment is similar to that in earlier human history.

ev.t: Maniq and Jahai speakers live in tropical rainforest regions with a hunting-gathering lifestyle
In an environment that is still largely untouched by humans
